newsitem.title: UK: Hanson to shake up US construction - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hanson to shake up US construction - paper.

text.p: Hanson Plc is planning a fundamental reorganisation of its U.S. construction operations, the Sunday Telegraph reported but Hanson's chief executive-elect told Reuters he was excited about prospects in the U.S.
Plans are expected to include rationalisation of Hanson's aggregates business and the possible sale or demerger of Spectrum, its contracting subsidiary, the Sunday Telegraph said.

It said Andrew Dougal, Hanson's new chief executive, had ordered a review of Cornerstone, its U.S. aggregates business. "We're very excited about prospects in the U.S., both in Grove (Worldwide) and Cornerstone," Dougal told Reuters.
"We want to play a leading part in the inevitable industry consolidation in the U.S.," he said. "The aggregates industry is far more fragmented than in Britain."
Dougal added that "great progress" had already been made at Cornerstone. "We've increased our level of investment in the business but feel we can go further."
He also said Hanson was increasing its profile in downstream products such as concrete products.

The Sunday Telegraph said the group is considering buying a one-off insurance policy to cover environmental liabilities. That would allow it to release much of the 1.7 billion stg provision on its balance sheet, it said.
"We're looking at it but whether we're successful in that area remains to be seen. It's too early to say," Dougal told Reuters. "But provisions will fall either way."

The Sunday Telegraph said Dougal has ruled out any major acquisitions for Hanson for the time being. But it reported that the Energy Group has raised an acquisition war chest of almost 1.1 billion pounds.
As part of a four-way demerger, Hanson hived off Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals in October and will float the Energy Group early in 1997.
The Sunday Telegraph said the Energy Group had sold a revenue stream from power stations it acquired from National Power and PowerGen for 1,097 million pounds, thus radically reducing its debts.
The paper said that leaves the group in position to acquire more electricity businesses, maybe in generating and possibly also in the United States. No company spokesman was available for comment.
